scope.summary: This standard specifies standard pressure ranges in starting-air and compressed-air systems of vessels for inland navigation. It defines standard nominal pressure values used to select equipment, machinery, and pipeline elements (such as air receivers, compressors, fittings, valves, and piping) to ensure the unification, standardization, and interchangeability of pneumatic systems in inland water transport.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / System Standard (Marine Engineering / Inland Waterways)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary System and Performance Specification. Unlike steel constructions, builders hardware, or hazardous fluid packaging which are subject to mandatory statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), IS 10527 : 1983 is certified on a voluntary basis. Shipyards and marine auxiliary manufacturers who satisfy the requirements are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on air receivers, manifolds, and control valves. However, compliance with this standard is universally mandated inside all national public sector (such as Inland Waterways Authority of India - IWAI), port authority, and commercial maritime vessel procurement tenders to ensure the safety and interchangeability of pneumatic machinery.

requirements.detail: The starting-air pressure ranges are intended strictly to guide the selection, sizing, and design of equipment, machinery, and pipeline elements (such as air receivers, compressors, fittings, and valves) for starting main and auxiliary propulsion engines or diesel generators.

The compressed-air pressure ranges cover equipment, machinery, and pipeline elements of auxiliary systems providing the operation of: blast signals, pneumatic tanks, windshield wipers, towing winch brakes, coupling locks, pneumatic control of main engines, air supply for domestic requirements, blowing Kingston valve boxes, casting off towing hooks, and releasing anchors.
Specifies nominal pressure ranges in kPa (kilopascals) for selection: 100, 125, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1500, 2000, 2500.
To maintain international consistency and simplify calculation methods across mechanical, hydraulic, and structural design disciplines, the standard defines that: 100 kPa = 1 kgf/cm².

All piping manifolds, high-pressure reservoirs, steel tubes, and connecting valves used in inland vessel air systems must be designed, dimensioned, and pressure-tested to match the selected nominal values of this standard, ensuring leak-proof sealing under extreme marine humidity and rocking stresses.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10527 : 1983 (Reaffirmed 2023) is the national Indian Standard specification governing standard pressure ranges for compressed-air and starting-air systems on inland navigation vessels. Based identically on ISO 3948:1977, this standard provides a unified series of nominal pressure values (such as 100, 200, 500, up to 2500 kPa) used to design and select marine pneumatic equipment, compressors, air receivers, control valves, and pipelines. It categorizes pressures into a 'Principal Series' for routine machinery operations (such as engine starting, blast signals, towing brakes, and anchor releases) and an 'Additional Series' for exceptional designs, standardizing the conversion factor of 100 kPa to 1 kgf/cm² to ensure complete engineering compatibility in the shipbuilding and river transport industries.
